reference.source: GeneReviews / Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: Arises from a microduplication of chromosome 17p11.2, the reciprocal of the deletion that causes Smith-Magenis syndrome
RAI1 is the dosage-sensitive gene at the locus, and its increased copy number drives much of the phenotype
Infancy is characterised by hypotonia, poor feeding, and failure to thrive, in contrast to the obesity tendency of Smith-Magenis syndrome
Autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, and language delay are common neurodevelopmental features
Cardiovascular anomalies, including structural heart defects, may be present and warrant screening
Sleep disturbance and behavioural difficulties are frequent, though the sleep pattern differs from the inverted circadian rhythm of Smith-Magenis syndrome
The behavioural and growth profile is broadly a mirror image of the deletion disorder at the same locus
Diagnosis is by chromosomal microarray demonstrating the 17p11.2 duplication
reference.pathophysiology: The syndrome is caused by a recurrent duplication of a segment of chromosome 17p11.2 generated by non-allelic homologous recombination between flanking low-copy repeats, the same architecture that produces the reciprocal Smith-Magenis deletion. The critical dosage-sensitive gene within the interval is RAI1, and having three functional copies rather than two disturbs the transcriptional programmes it regulates, affecting neurodevelopment, growth, feeding, and circadian behaviour. Because the phenotype reflects gene over-dosage rather than haploinsufficiency, many features present as the clinical opposite of Smith-Magenis syndrome, such as the poor early growth seen in place of obesity. Additional genes within the variably sized duplication may modify the presentation.
additionalDifferentials: Smith-Magenis syndrome, the reciprocal deletion disorder at the same locus
Autism spectrum disorder of other genetic or idiopathic cause
Other copy-number neurodevelopmental syndromes detected on microarray
Syndromic causes of neonatal hypotonia and failure to thrive
Fragile X syndrome in males with intellectual disability and autism
Congenital heart disease with associated developmental delay
additionalInvestigations: Chromosomal microarray to confirm the 17p11.2 duplication and define its extent
Echocardiography to detect structural cardiac anomalies
Feeding and growth evaluation in infancy
Sleep assessment where sleep disturbance is prominent
Parental testing to establish whether the duplication is de novo or inherited
redFlags: Failure to thrive with inadequate weight gain in infancy requiring nutritional support
reference.prognosis: Most individuals have a normal lifespan, with the long-term picture dominated by intellectual disability, autism spectrum features, and behavioural and sleep difficulties; early feeding and growth problems often improve with support, and the overall outlook depends on the severity of neurodevelopmental involvement and any associated cardiac disease.
pitfalls: Expecting the obesity and self-injurious behaviours of Smith-Magenis syndrome and thereby overlooking the reciprocal duplication
Relying on karyotype, which lacks the resolution to detect this microduplication
Attributing feeding failure solely to non-genetic causes and delaying microarray testing
Neglecting cardiac screening in an infant with the duplication
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: No disease-specific therapy exists; care centres on early developmental intervention with speech and language therapy, occupational therapy and physiotherapy for hypotonia and delay
Feeding and nutritional support in infancy, including dietetic input and supplemental (nasogastric) feeding, to address poor feeding and failure to thrive
Echocardiographic screening and cardiology management of any structural cardiac anomaly
Behavioural and individualised educational support for autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability
Assessment and management of sleep disturbance, with a sleep study where indicated
Multidisciplinary follow-up across clinical genetics, paediatrics, cardiology and developmental services
Genetic counselling with parental chromosomal microarray to determine whether the duplication is de novo or inherited and to advise recurrence risk
